title: Double sale: Article 1544
description: Requisites, the priority ladder, good faith, and competing-claims warnings.

blocks.markdown: **The indispensable first question.** Article 1544 applies only when **the same seller makes two or more valid sales of exactly the same property** to different buyers whose claims conflict. If one transaction is only a contract to sell, or if the purported sales come from different vendors without authority linking them, the double-sale rule may not apply.

table.caption: The Art. 1544 priority ladder
rows: The buyer who first takes possession in good faith.
Prove possession and good faith; possession must be the legally relevant possession.
The buyer who in good faith first records the acquisition in the Registry of Property.
Registration must be in good faith; a buyer aware of the prior sale cannot win simply by registering first.
The buyer who in good faith is first in possession.
Possession and good faith must be established.
The buyer who presents the oldest title, provided there is good faith.
Oldest title is the last fallback, not the first rule.

blocks.markdown: The familiar phrase “first in time, first in right” is **not** the actual sequence in Art. 1544. For immovables, **good-faith registration is first**; only if there is no inscription do possession and then oldest title matter.
